stories.title: Planning for international university applications
stories.summary: Getting into prestigious universities abroad requires more than high grades. Students aiming for Ivy League or top UK institutions should begin preparation well before deadlines. Universities expect strong academic records, recommendation letters, and carefully crafted essays that demonstrate a student's specific interests and abilities.

stories.title: Vietnamese student chooses South Korea over US
stories.summary: Hoang Huong Giang, a student with a perfect SAT score, chose KAIST in South Korea over prestigious US and European universities. She cited the environment for studying artificial intelligence and computer engineering as her primary motivation. She is currently focusing on her research interests.

stories.title: Federal judge dismisses Stanford student visa case
stories.summary: A federal judge dismissed a lawsuit filed by a Stanford doctoral student seeking to resolve a stalled visa renewal. The court ruled it lacks the legal power to intervene in State Department consular processes. The student has been in limbo since May 2025.

stories.title: International students report rising visa anxiety
stories.summary: International students at Vassar College are reporting increased anxiety regarding travel, visa uncertainty, and a tightening job market. Students are navigating these challenges as national visa policies undergo revisions. The college international population remains just under 10 percent of the total student body.

stories.title: Australia consults on international student visa reforms
stories.summary: The Australian government is revising processes for the Genuine Student test and strengthening financial requirements to discourage visa hopping. Assistant Minister Julian Hill announced the consultation following high visa refusal rates. Stakeholders are invited to provide feedback on the proposed policy changes.

stories.title: IDP Education faces visa policy headwinds
stories.summary: IDP Education is currently being assessed on whether international student demand can recover from recent policy changes. The firm is navigating shifts in Australian education policy and visa settings. The next formal update is expected to clarify the impact on its counselling and testing business.

stories.title: US midterm elections and international students
stories.summary: Democrats have secured control of both chambers of Congress, flipping key seats in states like Kansas. The result arrives as the Trump administration continues to restrict opportunities for international students. Miriam Feldblum of the Presidents Alliance said the results underscored that voters are paying attention to fairness.

stories.title: Philippines to fast-track student visas
stories.summary: The Commission on Higher Education is launching a strategy to slash bureaucracy and make the arrival of international students effortless. Modelled on a Malaysian system, the initiative aims to create a roadmap for mobility. The Philippines is driving talent attraction to become a vibrant destination for academics.

stories.title: Australia considers student bank deposit requirements
stories.summary: The Australian government is seeking input on a proposal requiring international students to deposit 50 to 100 percent of tuition fees into a local bank account before applying for a visa. The plan has raised concerns about financial risks if an application is ultimately rejected.

stories.title: Australia offers two-year training visa
stories.summary: Australia is offering a subclass 407 training visa allowing foreign nationals to undertake supervised workplace training for up to two years. The program targets people seeking professional development or skills needed in their home countries. Applicants must secure an approved sponsor and meet English language requirements.

stories.title: Immigration policy after the US midterms
stories.summary: Democrats have taken control of the House and Senate, promising greater scrutiny of the Trump administration immigration agenda. However, with executive powers intact and court battles ongoing, H-1B workers and international students may have to wait for relief. The balance of power in Washington has shifted.

stories.title: Punjab government launches free civil services coaching
stories.summary: The Punjab government is providing free online coaching for UPSC and PCS examinations to 1,000 college students. The program, led by Education Minister Harjot Bains, covers 750 students from government colleges and 250 from private institutions. The initiative aims to make competitive exam preparation accessible to all.

stories.title: Collaboratory opens 2027 scholarship applications
stories.summary: Collaboratory is accepting scholarship applications for its 2027 funding cycle. The program supports high school seniors, adult learners, and students pursuing technical or graduate degrees. Residents of Charlotte, Collier, Glades, Hendry, and Lee counties may apply through January 14, 2027. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Front Royal utility offers student scholarship
stories.summary: Graduating seniors in Front Royal can apply for a 3,000 dollar Lyle B. Wright Scholarship. The program is available to students whose households receive electricity from the town municipal utility. Applications are due December 16, 2026. The scholarship encourages students to consider careers in the utility industry.

stories.title: New scholarship fund for Wayne County students
stories.summary: Upward Bound Youth has established a 1 million dollar scholarship fund with the Wayne County Community Foundation to help students of faith pay for college. The fund will initially award two students 5,000 dollars each, with the possibility of renewal for up to four years.

stories.title: Wageningen University offers master scholarships
stories.summary: Wageningen University and Research is offering scholarship programs for international students seeking to join its Master classroom for the 2027 to 2028 academic year. The university noted that funding remains one of the most important factors for students considering an international education.

stories.title: The Woodlands Arts Council opens scholarship applications
stories.summary: The Woodlands Arts Council is accepting applications for its 2027 Student Art Scholarship Program, offering graduating seniors up to 8,000 dollars. Students must submit a portfolio of three original works in 2D, 3D, or literary art. Applications remain open until January 5, 2027.

stories.title: Denmark offers environmental sustainability internship
stories.summary: The Scan Design Foundation is offering 12 fully funded spots for a 2027 environmental sustainability internship in Copenhagen. The program is open to US undergraduate and graduate students. Applications for the immersive professional and cultural experience close on November 20, 2026.

stories.title: UNICEF offers AI internship in Italy
stories.summary: UNICEF is accepting applications for a paid, full-time artificial intelligence internship based in Rome. The 26-week program is open to university students and recent graduates interested in digital transformation and fundraising. Applications for the position close on November 14, 2026.

stories.title: HSE University offers tuition-free master scholarships
stories.summary: The Higher School of Economics University is hosting an international olympiad for students seeking tuition-free master degree study in Russia. The online academic competition covers 128 academic fields. Outstanding participants may receive consideration for quota-based admission places at the university.

stories.title: King College London offers joint PhD scholarships
stories.summary: King College London is inviting applications for 2027 to 2028 joint PhD scholarships. The program offers full tuition coverage, an annual living stipend, and up to 5,000 pounds in research funding. The scholarship supports academic collaboration between the university and four international partners.

stories.title: Nagaland launches education reform initiative
stories.summary: Nagaland has set an initial target to engage 1,000 students in the One Million Voices initiative, a movement collecting youth views on education reforms. Advisor Dr Kekhrielhoulie Yhome stated the state may expand the target to 2,500 students to better understand the challenges facing young people.

stories.title: UCT MBA ranks second in global sustainability list
stories.summary: The University of Cape Town MBA programme climbed five places to reach second globally in the 2026 Corporate Knights Better World MBA Ranking. The school finished ahead of Australia’s Griffith Business School, which held the top spot for six years. Maastricht University claimed first place this year.

stories.title: GBPUAT enters QS Asia University Rankings
stories.summary: Govind Ballabh Pant University of Agriculture and Technology has secured a place in the QS Asia University Rankings 2027. Vice-chancellor Shivendra Kumar Kashyap said the university aims to provide new dimensions to agricultural education and enhance farmers income through scientific research. The institution is India's first agricultural university.

stories.title: LPU climbs in QS Asia rankings
stories.summary: Lovely Professional University has risen 33 places to rank 154th in the QS World University Rankings Asia 2027. The university claims its performance places it ahead of several Indian Institutes of Technology. It also secured the 15th position in Asia for its international research network indicator.

stories.summary: Kazakhstan remains the only Central Asian country with universities in the top 100 of the QS Asia rankings, though its three leading institutions all fell. Al-Farabi Kazakh National University dropped to 46th, while the nation increased its total representation to 51 universities across the regional list.

stories.summary: The QS World University Rankings Asia 2027 evaluated 1,722 institutions across 26 education systems. The University of Hong Kong took the top spot, followed by Peking and Tsinghua universities. India fielded 325 ranked universities, with IIT Delhi leading the national cohort at 66th place.

stories.title: Top Indian universities drop in QS Asia rankings
stories.summary: India's leading higher education institutions have seen a decline in the latest QS Asia rankings. IIT Delhi remains the highest-ranked Indian institution but fell from 59th to 66th place. Other top institutions including IISc Bengaluru and several IITs also slipped from their previous positions.

stories.title: Bihar imposes social media rules for schools
stories.summary: The Bihar government has banned teachers and students from uploading social media reels without permission. This follows a new formal dress code enforced in October. The state manages over 76,000 government schools, which have recently faced scrutiny regarding their operational conditions and overall performance.

stories.title: SRFTI campus closure extended
stories.summary: Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute has extended its campus closure until December 11. The institute has faced ongoing protests since September 27 following alleged attacks on students during an event. Protesting students have accused the administration of using coercive measures to manage the campus crisis.

stories.title: Government to review UGC equity regulations
stories.summary: The Centre told the Supreme Court it is forming a committee to re-examine the UGC 2026 equity regulations. The rules were designed to prevent discrimination in universities, but triggered protests from students and parents. The government is now reconsidering the framework following a nationwide uproar.

We introduce AraEngage, a query-defined sample of 10,000 public Arabic Facebook news posts from 2,451 pages in. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Coding with the Enemy: Can Human Developers Detect AI Agent Sabotage?
research.summary: Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: AI coding agents are increasingly embedded in real-world software development, collaborating with human developers while gaining broader access to codebases and tools. This creates a new attack surface: an agent can exploit human trust to sabotage. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Digital Security Under Compound Threats: Surveillance, Threat Reasoning, and Habituation Among North Korean Defectors in China
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: North Korean defectors residing in China face persistent uncertainty regarding digital security and privacy. Through semi-structured interviews with 19 defectors, we examine how individuals understand digital threats and adapt their security behaviors. We identify three interrelated. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
